title: A Uyghur herders' village flooded and demolished for the Ertanggou reservoir
place: Tuyamar village, Qialekan administrative village, Shanshan County, Turpan, Xinjiang, China

lenders.name: World Bank (IBRD)
lenders.role: Project P111163, loan IBRD-79340 of US$100 million for the Xinjiang Turfan Water Conservation Project, approved 17 June 2010, effective 28 October 2010, closed 31 March 2017; the full US$100 million was disbursed. Environmental category A. Seven safeguard policies were triggered: environmental assessment OP 4.01, natural habitats OP 4.04, pest management OP 4.09, physical cultural resources OP 4.11, indigenous peoples OP 4.10, involuntary resettlement OP 4.12 and safety of dams OP 4.37. The Bank's completion report of 13 October 2017 rates the outcome Highly Satisfactory, Bank performance Satisfactory, borrower performance Satisfactory, and risk to the development outcome Moderate. The Independent Evaluation Group's review of 22 November 2017 agrees on the first four ratings and prints the risk rating as Modest.

companies.name: Turpan Prefecture Water Resources Bureau
companies.role: Implementing agency, the prefectural water authority in Xinjiang; its project management office ran the works. The resettlement itself was carried out by the Shanshan County government, which set up a project leading group and a resettlement office for it. No construction contractor is named in the documents.

community: The project built three reservoirs to store water upstream: Alagou, Meiyaogou and Ertanggou. The Ertanggou reservoir flooded a hamlet called Tuyamar village, known as the Ertanggou villager group of Qialekan administrative village. The Bank's completion report says the reservoir affected 103 people in 26 households, all of them Uyghur herders, and that the whole village was inundated and the houses demolished. The report prints an inundation inventory of 4,774.36 square metres of houses, 14.11 mu of arable land, 21.37 mu of orchard, 35.05 mu of man-made pasture, 700 mu of natural pasture, 167.86 mu of forestry land, 2.5 kilometres of pasture road and one hydrological station. Every figure in that table also stands, to the decimal, in the reservoir’s 2009 resettlement plan, where the housing line reads "the area of houses which will be resettled is 4774.36 m2". The report gives the table as impact and the plan gives it as forecast, and no document says the two were measured again at the end. Four more households who lived outside the village but owned assets in it are counted inside the 103. Nobody living around the Alagou and Meiyaogou reservoirs was affected, and a few trees and other assets lost there were compensated. Shanshan County built a new site 15 kilometres away in a Uyghur neighbourhood, with 29 house yards of 1,300 square metres each, water and power, a road, a small clinic, a grocery store, a new mosque and an enlarged primary school in the next village. Each household was given a set of furniture worth RMB 5,000. For the resettlers' livelihoods, 14 hectares of desert land was reclaimed at the new site and 818 metres of irrigation canals were built; the report says the soil was highly saline at first and the households were given technical help with it. The report says their living standards were restored and improved and that they were satisfied with the compensation. A survey of 10 of the 26 households by the project's outside monitor puts average household income at RMB 41,646 in 2014 against RMB 28,175 before the move.
outcome: The project closed on 31 March 2017. The completion report's cost table gives the resettlement as budgeted at 22,156.8 thousand yuan and spent at 20,229.7 thousand yuan, with the rural resettlement line itself spending more than planned and other lines less. Shanshan County added Y27.63 million of its own for housing and productive infrastructure at the new site, which the report says brought the total to Y47.86 million, double the original budget. The report says the herders had stopped pasturing with a subsidy of RMB 3,500 a person a year, and attributes that pause to a hill-closure campaign for ecological rehabilitation run by Turpan Prefecture rather than to the project. A new pasture road was built along the mountains at the herders' request.

lenders.role: Project P091949, loan IBRD-75420 of US$38.40 million for the Gansu Cultural and Natural Heritage Protection and Development Project, approved 20 March 2008, effective 11 August 2008, closed 30 June 2015 after two restructurings; US$35.02 million was disbursed. The Bank's completion report gives the finished figures for both together: 14 households relocated, 19.54 mu of land permanently acquired and 870.71 square metres of housing pulled down, with 26 households and 123 people affected either permanently or temporarily. companies.role: Implementing agency, the provincial body for inland waterway navigation in Jiangxi; the Jiangxi Project Management Office sat within it and ran the land acquisition and resettlement with the county governments. No construction contractor is named in the documents.

title: Late compensation for 2,411 people and a safety suspension on the Grand-Bassam–Aboisso–Noé road works
place: Noé, Aboisso, Assouba, Samo and Port-Bouët, along the Grand-Bassam–Aboisso–Noé road, Côte d’Ivoire

lenders.name: World Bank (IDA)
lenders.role: Second Phase Project of the Abidjan-Lagos Trade and Transport Facilitation Program (P116323), IDA grant H7870 of SDR 57.9 million (US$90 million equivalent) to the Republic of Côte d’Ivoire; Board approval 31 May 2012, actual closing 29 March 2019 (completion report ICR00004935, 18 December 2019; evaluation review ICRR0021995, 5 June 2020). The Bank partly suspended disbursements on Component B from December 2016 after safety and resettlement failures. The completion report rates the overall outcome Moderately Satisfactory (ICR00004935, paragraph 47); the Independent Evaluation Group also rates the outcome Moderately Satisfactory (ICRR0021995).

companies.name: Projet de Facilitation du Commerce et du Transport sur le Corridor Abidjan-Lagos (PFCTCAL) Project Implementation Unit
companies.role: Implementing agency named in the completion report. companies.name: Ghana Highway Authority
companies.role: Road agency of Ghana’s Ministry of Roads and Highways, through its Road Safety and Environment Division; wrote the abbreviated resettlement plan for the 640 m dual carriageway and Noé bridge on the Ghanaian side, disclosed under the same project number in December 2017

community: The completion report records 2,411 people affected by the works of Component B. Of those, 2,256 were compensated, which it puts at 94 per cent, and 155 could not be reached. FCFA 3.6 billion (US$7.2 million) was spent on the resettlement plan, of which FCFA 3.5 billion, 98 per cent, went directly to affected people and FCFA 56 million was placed in an escrow account. The affected people were at Port-Bouët, Samo, Assouba, Aboisso and Noé. The report says counterpart money had been set aside at appraisal so that everyone would be paid before civil works started, “however compensations were carried out with delays”, and that civil works went ahead while the resettlement plan had not been fully carried out four years into the project. At Noé the project built a platform of 8,800 square metres to move the affected traders onto; a Noé Traders Management Committee set up by Ministerial Order in June 2019 runs the new market. The borrower’s own report, printed in the completion report, says the resettlement of Noé’s traders after compensation “preserves the activities of the people affected by the project”, and that the works at the Noé parking lot were provisionally finished but had defects. On the Ghanaian side of the same crossing, the abbreviated resettlement plan of December 2017 sets a cut-off date of 19 October 2015 and counts 38 “total affected household heads/PAPs who will be losing structures and crops”, with compensation valued at GH¢389,513.95 (US$88,525.90). Payment is the responsibility of the Government of Ghana: the plan says the Ministry of Finance had already released the funds to the Ghana Highway Authority, pending the Bank’s approval of the plan. Two years after the cut-off date the plan records that “the PAPs have already stopped farming after the notification of the cut-off date”, that “continuous consultations have been going on to update the PAPs on the delay in the implementation of the RAP”, and that site visits on 27 to 29 November and 5 December 2017 found no new cocoa trees or other crops planted and nothing changed on the ground since the cut-off date, although planting around the houses had continued by agreement with the affected people until they were paid.
outcome: The suspension was lifted after a nine-point action plan that moved project management to a new unit, added an environmental and a social specialist, and ordered safeguards, technical and safety audits. The road condition was improved on 113.59 km against a target of 130.3 km. The completion report says the overall safeguards were rated Moderately Unsatisfactory “during a significant period of implementation”, and that some of the accidents had led to protests from local communities.
